title: Bolted L-bracket, inside fillet r = 5 mm
description:
Bolted steel angle bracket (L-bracket) with a transverse load on its upright leg. 3D solid.
Geometry file (STEP): the full bracket in mm-scale dimensions written in metres.
Purpose: a machined L-bracket of constant thickness 8 mm and width 50 mm (y from 0 to 50 mm). The base leg lies on z = 0 .. 8 mm and extends from x = 0 to x = 80 mm; the upright leg lies on x = 0 .. 8 mm and rises from z = 0 to z = 60 mm. The outside corner (x = 0, z = 0) is square. The inside corner between the legs is blended by a fillet of radius r = 5 mm (axis along y, tangent to the top face of the base leg z = 8 mm and the inner face of the upright x = 8 mm). Two through holes of diameter 9 mm (M8 bolt clearance) pass vertically through the base leg, centred at (x, y) = (55 mm, 13 mm) and (55 mm, 37 mm).
Material: steel, linear elastic and isotropic, E = 200 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.3.
Supports: the base leg is bolted down; model the bolts by fixing the two bolt-hole bores (the cylindrical hole surfaces): all displacement components zero there.
Load: a total force of 1 kN in the -x direction (pulling the upright away from the base leg, opening the angle), uniformly distributed over the top end face of the upright leg (the face z = 60 mm).
Analysis: linear static, small displacements.
Report:
  max_vm_corner: the maximum von Mises stress on the fillet surface [Pa];
  load_displacement: the average x-displacement of the loaded face z = 60 mm [m].
